 STATE OF GUJARAT-FOR & ON BEHALF OF S A PATEL,FOOD  INSPECTOR  Versus  ABDULKADAR MOHMMEDJAMAL HARADVALA =============================================
Appearance:

MR KL PANDYA, ADDL. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR(2) for the PETITIONER(s) No. 1 MR DK MODI(1317) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 1,2,5,6,7 MR MD MODI(1318) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 1,2,5,6,7 RULE SERVED(64) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 3,4 =============================================
CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE G.R.UDHWANI State Of Gujarat-For & On Behalf Of S A ... vs Abdulkadar Mohmmedjamal Haradvala on 26 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77058516/

ORAL JUDGMENT 1. Judgment and order dated 31.03.2010 rendered by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Himmatnagar in Criminal Case No.147 of 2007 recording acquittal for the respondents for the offences punishable under Sections 7(1) and 7(5) of the Prevention R/CR.A/1515/2010 JUDGMENT of Food Adulteration Act, 1955 (for short 'Act') has been assailed in this Appeal under Section 378 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (for short Cr.P.C.).
2. The Food Inspector raided the proprietary concern of original accused nos. 1, 2 and 3 and collected samples of edible coconut oil from the packaged container weighing 5 kg.

on 22.06.2005,
which was reported to be adulterated in the report of the public analyst at Exh.-40.
3. On the label of the packaged food article several details including the marketer of the food article namely, Indu Oil Company were found.

When the Food Inspector made inquiry under Section 14A from the vendor of the food article, he learnt that the same was purchased by him from Sheth Enterprise and on inquiry with Sheth Enterprise he learnt that it was purchased from Sheth Oil Industries.

Sheth Oil Industries further came out with a case that the food article marketed by Indu Oil Company was not sold by it to Sheth Enterpise but the one marketed by Thirumalai Agencies was sold by it to Sheth Enterprise.
In other words, it was case of the Sheth Oil Industries that the food article in question was not sold by it to Sheth Enterprise.
4. The Food Inspector did not receive any co-operation from Indu Oil Company even as he kept on inquiring on four or five occasions with the said company, under Section 14A of the Act.

Eventually,
he filed the complaint.

5. Learned APP has assailed the impugned judgment and order on the ground that none of the entities above referred were entitled to the benefit under Section 14A in absence of their giving R/CR.A/1515/2010 JUDGMENT complete information with batch number and other facts leading to the identity of the food article in question, to the Food Inspector.
It was contended that Sheth Oil Industries took the stand above referred only to save Indu Oil Company and the Indu Oil Company did not come out with any details under Section 14A of the Act.

5.1 It was contended that the Court erroneously found that the sanction suffers from non-application of mind inasmuch as on not less than three occasions the authority after looking into the papers declined sanction and eventually when it found that no case is made out against Thirumalai Agencies, it refused the sanction qua the said entity and granted it for prosecuting other entities.
6.

Learned counsel for the respondents while urging for the sustainance of the impugned judgment and order would contend that whole quantity of 5 kg. of the food article i.e. coconut oil was not throughly stirred and thus the sample was not a representative sample and the accused must be given the benefit of doubt as indicated in Criminal Revision Application No.593 of 2005 [2008 (1)
FAC 381].

sentences.text: It was also contended that in absence of joining the manufacturer the complaint was not maintainable.

The learned counsel also contended that the food article could have been best used within 12 months from the date of manufacture and the sample was collected on 09.08.2004 and the complaint was lodged only on 15.02.2007 and by the time the best before date had gone and the food article was no more good for human consumption and therefore, the right of the respondents to get the sample re- analyzed as contemplated in Section 13(2B) of the Act, has been denied.
R/CR.A/1515/2010 JUDGMENT 7.
It is unnecessary to deal with all the arguments above referred except the one assailing the procedure of collecting the sample under Rule 14 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules.

It is noticed from the evidence of the Food Inspector - Prosecution Witness-1 that after unsealing the container of the packaged food article weighing 5 kg. he purchased therefrom 500 grams of the food article which was then divided into three samples.
No statement is made by him that the whole content of the said 5 kg. was stirred.
Neither there is any statement that before dividing the sample into three parts it was stirred.

The settled legal position that the sample needs to be stirred can be noticed in State of Gujarat Vs. Gamnaji Bhuraji Prajapati [Criminal Appeal No.1883 of 2004]
decided on 04.07.2006, State of Gujarat Vs. Laghadhirbhai Vaghjibhai Prajapati [2008 (1) FAC 381], Criminal Revision Application No. 593 of 2005 with Criminal Revision Application No. 594 of 2005 Kiritkumar Narandas Datani & 2 Others Vs. State of Gujarat & 1 Another decided on 23.04.2015.

sentences.text: 8. In absence of the stirring of the food article like coconut oil before collection of the sample, the sample cannot be said to be representative in character and in such a case there would be non- compliance with Rule 14 of the PFA Rules.
9. In above view of the matter, this Court is unable to find any cause for interfering in the acquittal recorded by the Court below.
The Appeal, therefore, fails and is accordingly dismissed.
(G.R.UDHWANI, J.)
